text.p: Placer Dome Inc said on Monday it had raised its stake in its takeover target Highlands Gold Ltd to 40.8 percent.
Placer Dome said it had received sufficient acceptances for its 75 cents a share on-market offer to take its shareholding to the 40.8 percent level.

"We are extremely pleased that Highlands Gold shareholders have seen the value in our offer and have almost rushed to accept," Placer Dome chief executive and president John Willson said in a statement.

"This highly encouraging response, coupled with the fact that we picked up 33.3 percent of the company in a matter of hours when we first launched our offer on market, sends a clear message that our offer is attractive," he said.

Placer Dome launched its offer for Highlands late last month but earlier this month said it was willing to cancel its interest in Highlands and instead pay A$276.8 million for Highlands' 25 percent stake in the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea.
Highlands has said it would consider the proposal over the Chrimas period and respond by January 6.

Prior to the new offer, Highlands had unanimously resolved to reject the takeover bid by Placer Dome, citing an independent report by Barings Bros Burrows showing Highlands shares to be worth about 40 percent more than Placer's offer.
Both companies have 25 percent stakes in Porgera, Placer's being held through its listed Placer Pacific Ltd unit, for which Placer Dome is also making a takeover offer.
The other equal 25 percent shareholders in Porgera are Goldfields Ltd and PNG interests.
The PNG interests are held 15 percent by Orogen Minerals Ltd and 10 percent by the government's Minerals Development Resources Corp (MRDC).
The MRDC holds five percent in its own right and five percent for provincial governments and landowners.
Highlands has estimated that production from the mine should total about 850,000 ounces of gold this year.
Highlands shares closed steady at 74 cents.
